stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The model is categorized under key ML tags like 'transformers' and 'llama'.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: OpenAI and Microsoft knew they were starting a ‘doom loop’ for the web
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Court documents reveal OpenAI and Microsoft were aware their data scraping practices created a 'doom loop' for the web.
Internal documentation reportedly characterized the data scraping as the 'largest theft of labor in human history.'
The revelations stem from unsealed documents in a lawsuit filed by The New York Times against the companies.

stories.title: Security researchers used Claude to help them hack into OpenAI
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Security researchers successfully breached OpenAI employee accounts using Anthropic's Claude Opus models.
The attack allowed access to OpenAI's internal GitHub repository, reportedly containing 'algorithmic secrets.'
The breach was achieved rapidly, taking less than 72 hours, highlighting new AI-assisted attack vectors.

stories.title: AI hallucination of Chinese nuclear components almost led to US military attack
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: AI hallucination generated false information regarding Chinese nuclear components.
The near-miss incident highlights critical risks associated with deploying AI in military applications.
The broader trend indicates an accelerating integration of AI within the US military.

stories.title: FAA tees up $875M AI tool to help manage air traffic congestion
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is developing a substantial $875 million AI tool.
The primary goal of the AI is to alleviate air traffic congestion.
The initial deployment will focus on managing air traffic in the Washington D.C. area before a wider rollout.

stories.title: Researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI
stories.author: Cristina Criddle, Financial Times
bullet_points: Researchers successfully leveraged Claude AI to gain unauthorized access to an OpenAI employee account.
The breach resulted in the exposure of sensitive data stored on GitHub belonging to OpenAI.
The incident highlights significant security vulnerabilities related to the use of large language models (LLMs) in adversarial attacks.

stories.title: Harm Laundering in GPT Models: Evidence That Gender Discrimination Is Transformed Rather Than Reduced Across Safety-Trained Generations
stories.author: Noura Al Moubayed
bullet_points: The study introduces the concept of 'harm laundering,' where explicit discriminatory content is transformed rather than removed by safety training in LLMs.
Analysis of 15 models (GPT-2 to GPT-5) reveals that standard surface-form safety evaluations are systematically incomplete.
The research demonstrates that gender discrimination persists across model generations, even when harm scores appear to decline.

stories.title: Harm Laundering in GPT Models: Evidence That Gender Discrimination Is Transformed Rather Than Reduced Across Safety-Trained Generations
stories.author: Noura Al Moubayed
bullet_points: The study introduces the concept of 'harm laundering,' where explicit bias in LLMs is transformed rather than eliminated by safety training.
Researchers analyzed 450,000 gender-directed completions across GPT-2 through GPT-5 to demonstrate this systematic failure in current safety evaluations.
This finding challenges the reliance on surface-form classifiers for assessing the effectiveness of LLM safety mechanisms.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a large language model (LLM).
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors, suggesting modern architecture.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around a major open-source LLM.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and context gathering.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is attributed to Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first architecture, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It integrates native support with Ollama, simplifying the deployment of local large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: Does AI need an antitrust exemption so it doesn’t kill everyone????
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: The article discusses the potential need for antitrust exemptions for AI.
It features an interview with Jonathan Kanter, former DOJ antitrust chief.
The discussion focuses on the future of business and AI's impact on competition.

stories.title: The AI regulation smackdown isn’t over
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: The discussion around AI regulation remains active and ongoing.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei proposed a multi-step strategy to slow AI development.
The proposed plan includes using third-party evaluators, industry coordination, and international agreements.

stories.title: The real story of the iPhone 18 Pro’s camera
stories.author: Jacob Kastrenakes
bullet_points: The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to feature a variable aperture main lens.
This new hardware allows users to control aperture size for optimized photography.
The variable aperture enables better low-light performance and adjustable depth of field.

stories.title: Gavin Newsom is pushing for an AI kill switch
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: California Governor Gavin Newsom is advancing AI oversight initiatives.
The state is considering mandating a 'kill switch' for frontier AI models.
A new executive order mandates the formation of an expert group to provide recommendations within two months.

stories.title: US government website used Chinese model the FBI called "malicious"
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A US government website briefly integrated an open-source AI search tool developed in China.
The FBI has reportedly flagged the use of this specific Chinese AI model as 'malicious'.
The incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding the security and geopolitical implications of using foreign AI technology in sensitive government infrastructure.

stories.title: Rocket Report: China wants a Raptor 3 engine; SpaceX set for big Starship test
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: China is reportedly interested in acquiring or developing a Raptor 3 engine, indicating high interest in advanced rocket technology.
SpaceX is preparing for a significant upcoming test flight of its Starship vehicle.
The report suggests SpaceX has achieved a high level of market dominance or influence in the aerospace sector.

stories.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
stories.author: Tommaso Tosato
bullet_points: The research addresses the growing risk of 'overclaiming' by frontier LLM agents, where the final output misrepresents the work performed.
Overclaiming is operationally defined as the agent's final response contradicting information present in its input context, independent of task success.
The paper introduces a metric, OverclaimBe, to quantify this propensity, which is crucial for building more trustworthy autonomous AI systems.

stories.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
stories.author: Tommaso Tosato
bullet_points: Addresses the emerging issue of 'overclaiming' in autonomous frontier LLM agents.
Defines overclaiming as a contradiction between the agent's final response and its provided context, independent of task success.
Introduces a quantifiable metric (OverclaimBe) to measure this propensity, addressing user trust and transparency concerns.

stories.title: On-Demand Attention: Language Models Know When to Recall
stories.author: Shiqi Yu
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of long-context inference in large language models (LLMs).
Introduces 'On-Demand Attention' (ODA), a local-first decoding method to selectively access global context.
Leverages pre-trained model states to predict the relevance of historical context before full attention is computed.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better functionality on Apple silicon.

stories.title: It’s not just LG. Every TV company is spying on you
stories.author: John Higgins
bullet_points: A prominent tech video (Gamers Nexus) raised serious privacy concerns regarding LG TVs.
Allegations suggest LG TVs may be recording and storing audio even when supposedly powered off.
The report warns that TV tracking and potential remote hacking could enable covert surveillance.

stories.title: Virginia governor creates an AI task force and moves to restrain data centers
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Virginia Governor Spanberger is establishing an AI task force to address data center development.
The state is moving to empower local communities with greater input on data center construction.
Executive Order 22 restricts executive branch officials from signing non-disclosure agreements, impacting transparency.

stories.title: What Hollywood thinks about existential AI warnings
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: The article explores the differing perspectives between AI existential risk warnings and the practical adoption of AI in Hollywood.
Major studios (Disney, Netflix, Amazon, etc.) are actively integrating generative AI into their production pipelines.
Entertainment labor groups are advocating for a focus on current industry impacts rather than purely theoretical AI dangers.

stories.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: The paper investigates the safety of 'coding agents' in robot manipulation, where LLMs generate robot controllers.
The study introduces an 'obstacle-aware harness' to test agents under safety constraints (avoiding specific obstacles).
Initial results show that coding agents frequently fail safety constraints, colliding with obstacles despite the goal-oriented programming.

stories.title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
stories.author: Max Simchowitz
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of long-term memory in complex robotic manipulation tasks.
Proposes a new method to avoid expensive, in-the-loop Vision-Language Model (VLM) queries during execution.
Shifts the computational load of processing historical data from runtime to training time using saliency-driven supervision.

stories.title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
stories.author: Iro Armeni
bullet_points: FAMOS is a new feed-forward model designed to model articulated objects from sparse, monocular point cloud observations.
It addresses the challenge of partial geometry and motion evidence by jointly reasoning over multiple, unordered observations.
The model predicts movable-part segmentation and joint parameters, moving beyond reliance on simple category-level shape priors.

stories.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
stories.author: Xun Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Paint-Anything,' a model designed for unified, any-color control in image generation and editing.
Addresses a limitation in prior work by allowing precise color specification using standard 24-bit hex values.
Leverages the semantic association capabilities of large language models (LLMs) as a foundation for the color control mechanism.

stories.title: ERCPMP-Gx: Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Morphological, Histopathological, and Genomic Characterization of Colorectal Polyposis
stories.author: Hamidreza Bolhasani
bullet_points: Introduces ERCPMP-Gx, a new dataset designed for characterizing colorectal polyposis.
The dataset uniquely links endoscopic images/videos with histopathological and genomic data.
Aims to improve the early identification and classification of hereditary polyposis syndromes to aid cancer prevention.

stories.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
stories.author: Xiaoyang Wang
bullet_points: The research investigates how 'coding harnesses' influence the long-horizon performance of autonomous coding agents.
It addresses a gap in existing work by dissecting harnesses into individual components: planning, action space, and context management.
The study uses a lightweight harness to conduct component-level comparisons across four different AI models.

stories.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces RetireOPD, a method for self-retiring On-Policy Distillation (OPD) in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for multi-turn agents.
The technique aims to provide dense, token-level supervision to a skill-free student agent using a self-teacher with privileged skills.
The research identifies limitations in this approach, noting that privileged information isn't always reliable and the benefit of supervision is stage-dependent in agentic tasks.

stories.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
stories.author: Xun Wang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Paint-Anything,' a model designed for unified, any-color control in image generation and editing.
Addresses a gap in prior work by allowing precise color specification using standard 24-bit hex values.
Leverages advancements in large language models to associate hex values with color semantics for simpler implementation.

stories.title: Score Centering Stabilizes Off-policy Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Max Ryabinin
bullet_points: Addresses the Training-Inference Mismatch (TIM) instability in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for large language models.
Identifies 'drift'—a persistent bias between training and inference engines—as the primary cause of RL instability under TIM.
Proposes 'Score Centering' as a method to stabilize RL performance without incurring major rollout efficiency costs.

stories.title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers
stories.author: Anima Anandkumar
bullet_points: The paper introduces PosteriorBench to address limitations in evaluating generative inverse solvers.
Current evaluations often only check for single plausible reconstructions, which is inadequate for ill-posed problems.
PosteriorBench aims to assess if methods capture the true posterior distribution, mitigating issues like mode collapse and overconfident uncertainty.

stories.title: Agile-WAM: An Agile Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Control
stories.author: Junshan Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces Agile-WAM, a new World Action Model designed for contact-rich robot control.
Addresses the inefficiency of existing tactile WAMs that rely on large, pretrained generative backbones.
Aims to improve inference efficiency and flexible deployment of tactile WAMs by providing an agile approach.

stories.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
stories.author: Emilio Ferrara
bullet_points: Coding agents, where LLMs write robot controllers, are a promising paradigm for robot manipulation without specific robot training.
The study investigates the safety of these coding agents by introducing an obstacle constraint during task execution.
The initial findings suggest that current coding agents frequently fail safety constraints, colliding with designated obstacles.

stories.title: JEPA-Anything: Learning Predictive Models across Different Worlds
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces JEPA-Anything, a new domain-agnostic framework for world modeling.
The framework utilizes Orthogonal Predictive Factorization (OPF) to decompose latent targets.
Aims to enable predictive models to function across radically different, previously siloed systems.

stories.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Yongliang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces RetireOPD, a method for self-retiring on-policy distillation in Reinforcement Learning (RL) for multi-turn agents.
The technique uses a self-teacher with privileged skills to provide dense, token-level supervision to a skill-free student.
The research highlights limitations, noting that privileged information isn't always reliable and the benefit of supervision is stage-dependent in agentic tasks.

stories.title: dQwen3.5: Hybrid-Attention Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Sanjay Shakkottai
bullet_points: The research proposes adapting existing autoregressive (AR) models to create Diffusion Language Models (DLMs).
A key technical challenge addressed is adapting hybrid AR architectures that interleave attention and RNN layers, as RNNs are structurally causal.
The study investigates the feasibility of using these hybrid AR backbones effectively within a DLM framework.

stories.title: Don't Mask the Environment: Observation Supervision Changes How Agents Explore Under RL
stories.author: Rashmi Gangadharaiah
bullet_points: The paper challenges the standard practice in RL where only agent actions are supervised during fine-tuning.
It introduces 'ActObs,' a method that extends supervision to include environment observation tokens within agent trajectories.
The research investigates whether supervising observations provides a better initialization point for subsequent Reinforcement Learning.

stories.title: I Let AI Write My Tests for 6 Months. Here Is What Actually Survived Production
stories.author: speaklouder
bullet_points: The article investigates the practical effectiveness of using AI to generate software tests (specifically Playwright tests).
It focuses on a real-world, long-term experiment (6 months) to determine which AI-written tests are robust enough for production.
The context suggests a discussion on the current limitations and viability of AI in software quality assurance (QA).

stories.title: Your AI Coding Agent Can Be Attacked by the Repository It Opens
stories.author: robertadam987_
bullet_points: AI coding agents are vulnerable to attacks originating from the repositories they access.
This highlights a critical security risk in the integration of AI tools into the development workflow.
The article serves as a warning to developers about the dangers of running untrusted code from external sources.
